# Psalm 123 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 123:1 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** A-song of-the-ascents. To-you I-lift my-eyes, the-one-dwelling in-the-heavens.
- **LOGOS:** A Song of Ascents. To you I lift up my eyes, O you who are enthroned in the heavens!
- **PNEUMA:** A song for the journey to Jerusalem. I look up to you — you who sit enthroned in heaven.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 123:4 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Greatly is-filled our-soul the-scorn-of the-at-ease, the-contempt-of the-proud.
- **LOGOS:** Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those who are at ease, of the contempt of the proud.
- **PNEUMA:** We're drowning in the mockery of the comfortable and the sneering of the arrogant.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 123:2 (overlap: 4%)

- **EMET:** Behold as-eyes-of servants to-hand-of their-master, as-eyes-of a-maidservant to-hand-of her-mistress, so our-eyes to-YHWH our-God, until he-is-gracious-to-us.
- **LOGOS:** Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maidservant to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the LORD our God, till he has mercy upon us.
- **PNEUMA:** Like servants watching their master's hand for a signal, like a maid watching her mistress — that's how we watch the LORD our God, waiting for him to show us mercy.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 123:3 (overlap: 8%)

- **EMET:** Be-gracious-to-us O-YHWH, be-gracious-to-us, for greatly we-are-filled-with contempt.
- **LOGOS:** Have mercy upon us, O LORD, have mercy upon us, for we have had more than enough of contempt.
- **PNEUMA:** Have mercy on us, LORD — have mercy! We've had more than our fill of contempt.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
